meta.description: Performs DESeq2 differential expression for bulk RNA-seq and donor-level single-cell pseudobulk counts, including Wald and LRT testing, LFC shrinkage, filtering, transformations, and paired, batch, and interaction designs.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: Every quantitative claim below was emitted by the saved deterministic synthetic runs or a shipped example; no fabricated research result was used.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill analyzes aggregate count matrices and does not diagnose, prescribe, or make clinical claims about an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: Fresh checks supported explicit contrasts, donor-level pseudobulk, LRT-only omnibus inference, and lfcThreshold instead of a post-hoc shrunken-LFC FDR claim.

code_usability.detail: All seven corrective inputs and all three shipped R examples exited 0 under isolated WSL micromamba environment deseq2-repair-20260923.

functional_suitability.note: The current description explicitly includes bulk and donor-level pseudobulk DE, and the decision tree covers the advertised contrasts, designs, transforms, filtering, and imports.

reliability.note: Failure modes and remedies are specific; all examined R routes now exit cleanly in the isolated runtime, though examples remain illustrative rather than fixture-tested.

performance_context.note: The concise SKILL.md delegates advanced topics to eleven clearly selected reference files.

agent_usability.note: The decision tree, named-coefficient warnings, and new reporting checklist give an agent clear execution and handoff guidance.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language now includes single-cell pseudobulk as well as bulk RNA-seq.

security.note: No credentials, destructive commands, or raw-code execution were found; count and metadata alignment is documented but not wrapped in a reusable validator.

maintainability.note: References are separated by method, all eleven referenced files exist, and all three shipped R examples parse and run.

agent_specific.note: Progressive disclosure, trigger precision, and scientific stop conditions are strong; the examples could expose machine-checkable expected outputs.

key_strengths: The branch-tip description now directly triggers for donor-level single-cell pseudobulk as well as bulk RNA-seq.
The new What to Report section specifies contrast, reference level, alpha, filters, sample counts, NA causes, and effect-size source.
All corrective data-analysis paths and all three shipped R examples completed with clean exit code 0 in the isolated WSL environment.
Live regressions confirmed the high-impact contrast, LRT, pseudobulk, filtering, and LFC-threshold safeguards.

recommendations.title: Add machine-checkable example expectations
recommendations.problem: The three shipped examples are runnable and completed cleanly, but they do not include asserted expected counts or result-shape checks for future drift detection.
recommendations.root_cause: The examples are intended as teaching scripts rather than regression fixtures.
recommendations.fix: When the Skill next changes, add lightweight deterministic assertions or a separate fixture-backed smoke script; no source change is required for this pass.
